title: Anand Kumar v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
coram: Surya Prakash Kesarwani, J. & Anish Kumar Gupta, J. (delivered by Anish Kumar Gupta, J.)
disposition: Writ petition disposed of (direction to process the tenant's connection application)
headnote: Under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 a 'premises' (Clause 2(ss)) is the specific portion for which a connection is sought, and a tenant is an 'occupier' (Clause 2(oo)) with a statutory right to apply for supply. The arrears-bar in the third proviso to Clause 4.1 operates only against dues on the same premises; by Clause 4.3(h) a licensee cannot refuse a new connection to an occupier of a distinct sub-premises on the ground that dues on other portions of the building are unpaid, and must instead pursue the defaulters under Clause 4.3(f)(v). A tenant may obtain a connection on an indemnity bond (Annexure 4.2, Clause 4.4) where the owner's consent is absent.

holding_units.topic: Arrears-bar is premises-specific; connection to a tenant/occupier of a distinct premises
holding_units.question: Can a licensee refuse a new connection to a tenant of a shop because of electricity dues outstanding against other portions of the same building?
holding_units.holding: No. The arrears-bar in the third proviso to Clause 4.1 applies only to dues on the same 'premises' (Clause 2(ss)); the shop is a distinct premises and the tenant is an 'occupier' (Clause 2(oo)) entitled to apply. Clause 4.3(h) forbids refusal on the ground of dues on other portions; the licensee must instead pursue the defaulters under Clause 4.3(f)(v).
holding_units.limiting_facts: No dues were specific to the shop occupied by the petitioner; the alleged dues were against other persons/portions of the building.

holding_units.topic: Tenant's connection on an indemnity bond absent owner's consent
holding_units.holding: Following Seema Mansoor, an occupier (including a tenant) has a statutory right to supply under Sections 42-43 read with Clause 4.4; where the owner's consent is unavailable, the tenant may file an indemnity bond (Annexure 4.2) to obtain the connection.

principle_tags.application: The bar on a new connection for arrears attaches only to the specific premises in default, not to other portions of a building.

not_decided.note: The Court expressly declined to record any finding on the landlord-tenant relationship; the direction is only to process the connection application after hearing the owner.

authorities.name: Seema Mansoor v. U.P. Power Corporation & 3 Others
authorities.proposition: An occupier (including a tenant) has a statutory right under Sections 42-43 and Clause 4.4 of the Code to apply for and obtain supply; where the owner's consent is absent, the indemnity-bond route (Annexure 4.2) is available.
authorities.how_treated: Followed and relied on to hold the tenant entitled to have the application processed.
